column1: # ieee1905 group, build A (note 0009 D7.1, B01). Builder A, 2026-11-20.
# Sources: IEEE 1905.1 through the usp-spec MCP server (doc ieee1905): §6.4 (TLV header), §6.4.2 Table 6-7,
#   §6.4.8 Table 6-14, §6.4.9 Table 6-15. TLV codes checked against 1905.1 tables and em-types codes.rs:242-252.
#   reserved bits), D3 lines 315/317, D4 (OUI-only vendor TLV is spec, not lenient).
# Wire layouts (hex = tlvValue only; multi-octet integers big-endian per 1905.1):
#   0x01: [0..6) AL MAC; exactly 6 (Table 6-8; audit 307 SPEC, note 0008 D8).
#   0x03: [0..6) AL MAC, [6] k, then k x { MAC(6), media type(2, BE), n(1), info(n) } (Table 6-10); k may be 0 (D2).
#         Info is raw bytes sized by n; media type vs n is not checked by the codec (D2). 802.11 info used here
#         per Table 6-13: BSSID(6), role in bits 7-4 + reserved bits 3-0 (1), apChannelBand(1), cf index1(1), cf index2(1).
#   0x04: [0] m, then m x { k(1), k x MAC(6) } (Table 6-11; L = m per D3 line 315); m and k may be 0 (D2).
#   0x06: [0..6) local MAC, then 0+ x neighbor MAC(6); no count octet, list length from tlvLength (Table 6-14; audit 316 SPEC).
#   0x07: [0..6) local MAC once, then 0+ x { neighbor AL MAC(6), flags(1): bit 7 bridge, bits 6-0 reserved }
#         (Table 6-15; D3 line 317, audit 318 SPEC). No count octet.
# Field notes: ifaces/tuples/neighbors are list lengths; for 0x06/0x07 they are not on the wire. if0_info_len overrides n.
#   `trailing`/`partial` are extra raw bytes appended after the listed fields. A field given as hex: where the
#   case normally takes a MAC/code is a cut field (raw bytes as written).
# Choices: every overstated count/length, cut field or partial entry is error=Truncated (InvalidLength is the
#   alternative). Empty 0x0b is invalid (a reachable upstream sender writes it, audit 304(a), but D4 lists no lenient form).
# media-80211-info-empty / media-0108-info-10 are spec bytes (D2: carried as found; audit 311 for 0x0108).
